en: Mencius prized plain virtue.
Shi Yu held to what is straight.
Close to the middle way.
Diligent, modest, careful and ordered.
Hear the sound, weigh the reason.
Read the face, discern the mood.
Bequeath good counsel.
Urge reverence and upright conduct.
Examine yourself and take warning.
Favor grows, pride peaks.
Disgrace and shame draw near.

meaning: 退居山林水边，幸而得之。
en: Retire to the woods and marsh, and be glad.
The two Shus saw the sign and withdrew.
Who forced them to untie the seal cords?
Living alone at leisure.
Silent and solitary.
Seek the ancients and their discourse.
Release cares and roam free.
Joy arrives, burdens leave.
Sorrow departs, gladness is called in.
Lotus in the ditch, bright and clear.
Shoots push up in the wild garden.
The loquat stays green late.
The paulownia sheds its leaves early.
Old roots wither and shade the ground.
Fallen leaves drift in the wind.
The great bird journeys alone.
Soaring up to the crimson sky.
Lost in books, amused by the market.
The eye rests on book bags and chests.
Light and easy matters are what to fear.
Ears pressed to the wall.
Meals are prepared.
Suit the taste, fill the belly.
Sated with cooked meat.
Hunger is eased with chaff and husks.
Kin and old friends.
Old and young eat different fare.
The women spin and weave.
Attending with towels in the inner rooms.
The silk fan, round and clean.
Silver candles blaze bright.
Nap by day, sleep at night.
Bamboo mat and ivory bed.
Strings and song, wine and feast.
Pass the cups and raise the goblets.
Lift hands and stamp feet to the music.
Joyful and in good health.
The direct line continues unbroken.
Offer the seasonal sacrifices.
Bow to the ground, twice over.
Trembling with fear.
Letters and records brief and clear.
Answer carefully and fully.
With a soiled body, one longs to bathe.
Holding something hot, one wishes for cool.
Donkeys, mules, calves and bulls.
Startled, leaping, racing ahead.
Thieves are struck down.
Rebels and runaways are seized.
Lu Bu's archery, Yiliao's juggling pellets.
Ji Kang's lute, Ruan Ji's whistling.
Meng Tian's brush, Cai Lun's paper.
Ma Jun's craft, the Ren master's fishing.
Settle disputes, benefit the world.
All are excellent and fine.
Mao Qiang and Xi Shi, beauties of old.
Even frowns are lovely, smiles are fair.
The arrow of years ever urges us on.
Sunlight shines clear and bright.
The armillary turns in the sky.
The dim moon circles and shines.
Pass the firewood on; cultivate blessing.
Ever at peace, auspicious and fair.
Square steps, head lifted high.
Bowing and rising in the court hall.
Belted up, grave and dignified.
Pacing about, gazing far away.
Isolated, shallow and ill-informed.
The foolish earn reproach alike.
As for the sentence particles —
— yan, zai, hu, ye.
